attachments.text:
NOTICE OF TERMINATION OF A LEASE FOR RESIDENTIAL PREMISES
Official form approved by the Canton of St. Gallen

Rented property: 3.5-room flat, 1st floor, Talstrasse 58, Rapperswil-Jona

The lease is terminated in writing with effect from: 31 October 2026

Reasons for the termination: will be stated on request.

Notes for the tenant: If you wish to contest this termination or request an extension of the lease, you must apply to the conciliation authority within 30 days of receiving this notice. The address of the competent conciliation authority is printed on the back of this form.

Place and date: Rapperswil-Jona, 3 May 2026

Signature of the landlord or its representative: (signed)

questions.label: Q1
questions.question: Does the notice or the claim state that the landlord terminated because the tenant did not pay overdue rent or accessory charges within a time limit the landlord had set?

questions.label: Q2
questions.question: Does the claim state that the tenant is married or in a registered partnership and that the rented dwelling serves as the family home?

questions.label: Q3
questions.question: Does the tenant seek an extension of the lease because having to leave by the end date would be a hardship for the tenant or the tenant's family?

questions.label: Q4
questions.question: Has the landlord given the tenant notice terminating the lease of the dwelling, and has it reached the tenant?

questions.label: Q5
questions.question: Does the claim state that the landlord gave notice because the tenant had, in good faith, asserted claims under the lease (for example demanded repair of a defect or contested the rent)?

text:
Hello,

My wife Isla Baumann and I got married in February 2023 and moved into the flat at Talstrasse 58 in Rapperswil-Jona that April. It has been our home as a married couple ever since, the place where we live together and where we planned to raise our family.

Then came a notice from Sonnbühl Property Ltd, dated 3 May 2026, terminating our lease. It arrived by registered post a couple of days later and I signed for it myself at the door.

The timing could hardly be worse. Isla is due to give birth in early October, which is exactly when we would have to be out. She has had a difficult pregnancy and her doctor has told her to avoid stress and heavy lifting. Flats in our price range (we pay CHF 1460 a month) are almost impossible to find around the lake, and we cannot realistically search, pack and move with a newborn. We would like the lease to be extended so we are not forced out at the worst possible moment, ideally until next summer.

I am convinced the real reason for the notice is my complaint from 15 January 2026. I wrote to Ms Kate Egli that the heating in the bedrooms had not worked properly all winter and asked for it to be repaired and for a reduction in the rent until it was fixed. That was a genuine problem, the radiators were cold for weeks. She was clearly irritated, and less than four months later we get the notice.

There is one more thing hanging over this. Ms Egli now says there was an unpaid heating charge of CHF 1365 and that she gave me a deadline to pay it before the notice went out. I don't remember any deadline, and we still disagree about whether that charge was ever properly owed. Whether this has anything to do with the termination, I really cannot say at this point.

I attach the notice itself. Please let me know what we can do.

Kind regards,
David Kaufmann
